title: Square of the radius of a circle
source: Theory P1-3.4 Quick check 1 (25); r^2 for integer radius
stem: Write down the value of \(r^2\) for the circle with centre \((2, -1)\) and radius \({r|int}\).

steps.name: A
steps.note: A is r squared. Original radius 5 gives 25.

title: Radius by completing the square
source: Theory P1-3.4 Quick check 2 (5); completing the square
stem: The equation of a circle is \(x^2+y^2-{p|int}x+{q|int}y-{c|int}=0\). Find the radius of the circle.

steps.name: A
steps.note: A is 5k. Original k=1 is x^2+y^2-6x+4y-12=0, radius 5.

title: Radius from the centre and a point
source: Theory P1-3.4 Quick check 3 (10); distance from the origin
stem: A circle has centre \((0, 0)\) and passes through the point \(({x|int}, {y|int})\). Find the radius of the circle.

steps.name: A
steps.note: A is 5k. Original k=2 gives the point (6, 8) and radius 10.

title: Equation of a circle given the centre and a point

source.note: 9709/12/O/N/20 Question 9(a) only [3]. Official QP and official MS. Part (b) omitted.

stem:
This question is 9709/12/O/N/20 Question 9(a) only, taken from the official QP.

A circle has centre at the point B (5, 1). The point A (−1, −2) lies on the circle.

(a) Find the equation of the circle. [3]

steps.name: R
steps.note: Official MS: B1, r = sqrt(6^2+3^2) or r^2=45 (sight of r=6.7 implies B1). Independent: (5-(-1))^2+(1-(-2))^2=36+9=45.

steps.name: M
steps.text_tex: \((x-5)^2+(y-1)^2=r^2\), using the given centre and their radius.
steps.note: Official MS: M1, using the centre given and their radius or an equivalent expanded form.

steps.name: A
steps.note: Official MS: A1. Do not allow a squared root written incorrectly for r.

contexts.note: Stem taken from the official QP PDF, Question 9(a) only. Official MS reproduced mark by mark. Paper/self-mark.
